   101→        if len(data['input'][session]) != ntrials:
   102→            errors.append(f"Session {session}: neural has {ntrials} trials but input has {len(data['input'][session])}")
   103→        if len(data['output'][session]) != ntrials:
   104→            errors.append(f"Session {session}: neural has {ntrials} trials but output has {len(data['output'][session])}")
   105→
   106→        if ntrials == 0:
   107→            warnings.append(f"Session {session} has 0 trials")
   108→            continue
   109→
   110→        # check that brain_region_idx are all ints between 0 and nbrain_regions-1
   111→        if not np.issubdtype(np.array(data['brain_region_idx'][session]).dtype, np.integer):
   112→            errors.append(f"Session {session}: brain_region_idx must be an array of integers")
   113→        if not (np.max(data['brain_region_idx'][session]) < nbrain_regions and np.min(data['brain_region_idx'][session]) >= 0):
   114→            errors.append(f"Session {session}: brain_region_idx contains invalid brain region indices")
   115→
   116→        nneurons_session = None
   117→        nneurons_mismatch = False
   118→        
   119→        # Check each trial
   120→        for trial in range(ntrials):
   121→
   122→            # Check that each trial is a numpy array
   123→            if not isinstance(data['neural'][session][trial], np.ndarray):
   124→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural must be numpy array, got {type(data['neural'][session][trial])}")
   125→                continue
   126→            if not isinstance(data['input'][session][trial], np.ndarray):
   127→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: input must be numpy array, got {type(data['input'][session][trial])}")
   128→                continue
   129→            if not isinstance(data['output'][session][trial], np.ndarray):
   130→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: output must be numpy array, got {type(data['output'][session][trial])}")
   131→                continue
   132→
   133→            neural_trial = data['neural'][session][trial]
   134→            input_trial = data['input'][session][trial]
   135→            output_trial = data['output'][session][trial]
   136→
   137→            # Check neural array shape (must be 2D)
   138→            if neural_trial.ndim != 2:
   139→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural must be 2D array (n_neurons, n_timepoints), got shape {neural_trial.shape}")
   140→                continue
   141→
   142→            # Check input array shape (1D or 2D)
   143→            if input_trial.ndim not in [1, 2]:
   144→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: input must be 1D or 2D array, got {input_trial.ndim}D with shape {input_trial.shape}")
   145→                continue
   146→
   147→            # Check output array shape (1D or 2D)
   148→            if output_trial.ndim not in [1, 2]:
   149→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: output must be 1D or 2D array, got {output_trial.ndim}D with shape {output_trial.shape}")
   150→                continue
   151→
   152→            # Get dimensions
   153→            n_neurons, T_neural = neural_trial.shape
   154→
   155→            # Check that number of neurons matches across session
   156→            if nneurons_session is None:
   157→                nneurons_session = n_neurons
   158→            else:
   159→                if nneurons_session != n_neurons:
   160→                    nneurons_mismatch = True
   161→
   162→            # Check that time dimensions match (for 2D input/output)
   163→            if input_trial.ndim == 2:
   164→                T_input = input_trial.shape[1]
   165→                if T_input != T_neural:
   166→                    errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural has {T_neural} timepoints but input has {T_input}")
   167→
   168→            if output_trial.ndim == 2:
   169→                T_output = output_trial.shape[1]
   170→                if T_output != T_neural:
   171→                    errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural has {T_neural} timepoints but output has {T_output}")
   172→
   173→            # Check data types
   174→            if not np.issubdtype(neural_trial.dtype, np.floating):
   175→                warnings.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural dtype is {neural_trial.dtype}, expected float32. Will be converted during training.")
   176→
   177→            if not np.issubdtype(input_trial.dtype, np.floating):
   178→                warnings.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: input dtype is {input_trial.dtype}, expected float32. Will be converted during training.")
   179→
   180→            # Output can be int or float
   181→            if not (np.issubdtype(output_trial.dtype, np.integer) or np.issubdtype(output_trial.dtype, np.floating)):
   182→                warnings.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: output dtype is {output_trial.dtype}, expected int or float")
   183→
   184→            # Check for NaN or Inf values
   185→            if np.any(np.isnan(neural_trial)) or np.any(np.isinf(neural_trial)):
   186→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: neural contains NaN or Inf values")
   187→            if np.any(np.isnan(input_trial)) or np.any(np.isinf(input_trial)):
   188→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: input contains NaN or Inf values")
   189→            if np.any(np.isnan(output_trial)) or np.any(np.isinf(output_trial)):
   190→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: output contains NaN or Inf values")
   191→
   192→            # Check if all neural data is zero
   193→            if np.all(neural_trial == 0):
   194→                warnings.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: all neural data is zero")
   195→
   196→            # check if whole dataset neural data is 0 and 1
   197→            if np.any(neural_trial != 0) or np.any(neural_trial != 1):
   198→                neural_is_all_01 = False
   199→
   200→            # check that dinput matches
   201→            if dinput is None:
   202→                dinput = input_trial.shape[0]
   203→            elif input_trial.shape[0] != dinput:
   204→                dinput_mismatch = True
   205→
   206→            # check that doutput matches
   207→            if doutput is None:
   208→                doutput = output_trial.shape[0]
   209→            elif output_trial.shape[0] != doutput:
   210→                doutput_mismatch = True
   211→                
   212→            # Check that output values are categorical (whole numbers)
   213→            if not np.allclose(output_trial, np.round(output_trial)):
   214→                errors.append(f"Session {session}, trial {trial}: output values must be categorical (whole numbers), found non-integer values")
   215→
   216→        if nneurons_mismatch:
   217→            errors.append(f"Number of neurons do not match across trials for session {session}")
   218→
   219→        if len(data['brain_region_idx'][session]) != nneurons_session:
   220→            errors.append(f"Length of brain_region_idx does not match number of neurons for session {session}")
   221→
   222→    # Check that input/output dimensions are consistent across all sessions
   223→    if dinput_mismatch:
   224→        errors.append(f"Trials do not all match in their input dimension")
   225→    if doutput_mismatch:
   226→        errors.append("Trials do not all match in their output dimension")
   227→    if neural_is_all_01:
   228→        errors.append("Neural data lacks variability. All values are 0 or 1")
   229→
   230→    if len(data['input_names']) != dinput:
   231→        errors.append("Length of input_names does not match dinput")
   232→
   233→    if len(data['output_names']) != doutput:
   234→        errors.append("Length of output_names does not match doutput")
   235→
   236→    if len(data['output_values']) != doutput:
   237→        errors.append("Length of output_values does not match doutput")
   238→
   239→    valid = len(errors) == 0
   240→    return valid, errors, warnings

   242→def get_dim(x: list):
   243→    """
   244→    Get the 0th dimension from the data.
   245→    Inputs:
   246→        x: list of length nsessions, x[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and x[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (d, T)
   247→    Returns:
   248→        d: int, dimension
   249→    """
   250→    ntrials_per_session = [len(x[session]) for session in range(len(x))]
   251→    session = np.nonzero(ntrials_per_session)[0][0]
   252→    d = x[session][0].shape[0]
   253→    return d
   254→
   255→def get_range(x: list):
   256→    """
   257→    Get the range of values across all sessions and trials.
   258→    Inputs:
   259→        x: list of length nsessions, x[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and x[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (d, T)
   260→    Returns:
   261→        min_x: numpy array of shape (dinput,), minimum input values
   262→        max_x: numpy array of shape (dinput,), maximum input values
   263→    """
   264→
   265→    d = get_dim(x)
   266→    min_x = np.zeros(d) + np.inf
   267→    max_x = np.zeros(d) - np.inf
   268→    for session in range(len(x)):
   269→        for trial in range(len(x[session])):
   270→            input_trial = x[session][trial]
   271→            if np.ndim(input_trial) == 1:
   272→                min_x = np.minimum(min_x, input_trial)
   273→                max_x = np.maximum(max_x, input_trial)
   274→            else:
   275→                min_x = np.minimum(min_x, input_trial.min(axis=1))
   276→                max_x = np.maximum(max_x, input_trial.max(axis=1))
   277→    return min_x, max_x

   479→def plot_trial(data: dict, session: int = 0, trial: int = 0, ax: list | None = None,
   480→               input_names: list | None = None, output_names: list | None = None,
   481→               predictions: list | None = None, nneurons_sample: int | None = None):
   482→    """
   483→    Plot neural, input, and output data for a specific trial of a specific session. If predictions are provided,
   484→    plot them alongside the true output.
   485→    Inputs:
   486→        data: dict with keys 'neural', 'input', 'output' as described in train_decoder.py
   487→        session: index of the session to plot, default = 0
   488→        trial: index of the trial to plot, default = 0
   489→        ax: optional list of matplotlib axes to plot on. If None, new figure and axes will be created.
   490→        input_names: optional list of length dinput with names for each input dimension
   491→        output_names: optional list of length doutput with names for each output dimension
   492→        predictions: optional list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
   493→                     predictions[session][trial] is a (doutput, T) array with predicted output for that trial,
   494→                     or None if no prediction exists for that trial.
   495→        nneurons_sample: optional integer, if provided, will sample this many neurons for plotting.
   496→    Returns:
   497→        fig: matplotlib figure
   498→        ax: list of matplotlib axes
   499→    """
   500→
   501→    if ax is None:
   502→        fig,ax = plt.subplots(3,1,figsize = (30,20),sharex=True)
   503→    else:
   504→        fig = ax[0].figure
   505→        
   506→    # neural

   509→        neuronstoplot = np.arange(nneurons)

   512→    for i, neuron in enumerate(neuronstoplot):
   513→        maxv = np.percentile(data['neural'][session][trial][neuron,:],99)
   514→        if maxv == 0:
   515→            maxv = 1.0
   516→        ax[0].plot(data['neural'][session][trial][neuron,:]/maxv+i)
   517→    ax[0].set_ylim((0,len(neuronstoplot)))
   518→    ax[0].set_ylabel('Neural')
   519→
   520→    dinput = data['input'][session][trial].shape[0]
   521→    T = data['neural'][session][trial].shape[1]
   522→    min_input, max_input = get_range(data['input'])
   523→    if np.ndim(data['input'][session][trial]) == 1:
   524→        input = np.tile(data['input'][session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))
   525→    else:

   576→def random_sample_trials(data, nsample, trial_indices=None):
   577→    """
   578→    Randomly sample trials across all sessions
   579→    Inputs:
   580→        data: dict with keys 'neural', 'input', 'output' as described in train_decoder.py
   581→        nsample: number of trials to sample
   582→        trial_indices: optional list of length nsessions, trial_indices[session] is a numpy array
   583→                       with valid trial indices for that session (e.g., test_indices from validate_decoder).
   584→                       If None, samples from all trials.
   585→    Returns:
   586→        sessionplot: numpy array of shape (nsample,), session indices for sampled trials
   587→        trialplot: numpy array of shape (nsample,), trial indices for sampled trials
   588→    """
   589→
   590→    nsessions = len(data['neural'])
   591→
   592→    if trial_indices is None:
   593→        # Sample from all trials
   594→        ntrials_per_session = [len(data['neural'][i]) for i in range(nsessions)]
   595→        valid_trials_per_session = [np.arange(n) for n in ntrials_per_session]
   596→    else:
   597→        # Sample only from specified trial indices
   598→        ntrials_per_session = [len(trial_indices[i]) for i in range(nsessions)]
   599→        valid_trials_per_session = trial_indices
   600→
   601→    # Sample sessions with equal probability
   602→    sessionplot = np.random.choice(nsessions, nsample, replace=nsample > nsessions)
   603→
   604→    trialplot = np.full((nsample,), -1, dtype=int)
   605→    for session in range(nsessions):
   606→        idx = session == sessionplot
   607→        ncurr = np.count_nonzero(idx)
   608→        if ncurr == 0:
   609→            continue
   610→        valid_trials = valid_trials_per_session[session]
   611→        if len(valid_trials) == 0:
   612→            continue
   613→        # Sample from valid trials and map back to original trial indices
   614→        sampled = np.random.choice(len(valid_trials), ncurr, replace=len(valid_trials) < ncurr)
   615→        trialplot[idx] = valid_trials[sampled]
   616→
   617→    return sessionplot, trialplot

   620→def _prepare_session_data(neural: list, input: list, output: list, device, doutput: int = None):
   621→    """
   622→    Helper function to prepare session data for training/validation.
   623→
   624→    Inputs:
   625→        neural: list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list of trials
   626→        input: list of length nsessions, input[session] is a list of trials
   627→        output: list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of trials
   628→        device: torch device to move data to
   629→        doutput: number of output dimensions (if None, inferred from data)
   630→
   631→    Returns:
   632→        session_data: list of dicts with 'neural', 'input', 'output', 'nneurons' tensors
   633→        dinput: input dimension
   634→        doutput: output dimension
   635→    """
   636→    nsessions = len(neural)
   637→
   638→    # Determine dimensions
   639→    # Find first non-empty session/trial
   640→    for sess in range(nsessions):
   641→        if len(neural[sess]) > 0:
   642→            if input[sess][0].ndim == 1:
   643→                dinput = len(input[sess][0])
   644→            else:
   645→                dinput = input[sess][0].shape[0]
   646→            if doutput is None:
   647→                if output[sess][0].ndim == 1:
   648→                    doutput = len(output[sess][0])
   649→                else:
   650→                    doutput = output[sess][0].shape[0]
   651→            break
   652→
   653→    # Process input/output: replicate 1D along time axis
   654→    input_processed = []
   655→    output_processed = []
   656→    for session in range(nsessions):
   657→        input_session = []
   658→        output_session = []
   659→        for trial in range(len(neural[session])):
   660→            T = neural[session][trial].shape[1]
   661→            if input[session][trial].ndim == 1:
   662→                input_trial = np.tile(input[session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))
   663→            else:
   664→                input_trial = input[session][trial]
   665→            input_session.append(input_trial)
   666→            if output[session][trial].ndim == 1:
   667→                output_trial = np.tile(output[session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))
   668→            else:
   669→                output_trial = output[session][trial]
   670→            output_session.append(output_trial)
   671→        input_processed.append(input_session)
   672→        output_processed.append(output_session)
   673→
   674→    # Create session data tensors
   675→    session_data = []
   676→    for session in range(nsessions):
   677→        if len(neural[session]) == 0:
   678→            session_data.append(None)
   679→            continue
   680→        neural_concat = np.concatenate([neural[session][trial].T.astype(np.float32) for trial in range(len(neural[session]))], axis=0)
   681→        input_concat = np.concatenate([input_processed[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(input_processed[session]))], axis=0).astype(np.float32)
   682→        output_concat = np.concatenate([output_processed[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(output_processed[session]))], axis=0).astype(np.int64)
   683→        session_data.append({
   684→            'neural': torch.from_numpy(neural_concat),
   685→            'input': torch.from_numpy(input_concat),
   686→            'output': torch.from_numpy(output_concat),
   687→            'nneurons': neural_concat.shape[1]
   688→        })
   689→
   690→    return session_data, dinput, doutput

   693→def train_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: dict = {}, **kwargs):
   694→    """
   695→    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.
   696→    Jointly learns projection matrices for each session and separate shared decoders for each output dimension.
   697→
   698→    Inputs:
   699→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list
   700→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),
   701→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial
   702→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of
   703→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
   704→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.
   705→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
   706→        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
   707→                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int with
   708→                categorical values for each timepoint. Each output[idx, t] is an integer from 0 to ncategories[idx]-1.
   709→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.
   710→
   711→        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:
   712→        npcs: number of projected dimensions to use (default: 10)
   713→        num_epochs: number of training epochs (default: 200)
   714→        lr: learning rate (default: 0.001)
   715→        l1_weight: L1 regularization weight for projection matrices (default: 1e-4)
   716→        svd_max_samples: maximum number of timepoints to use for SVD initialization (default: 50000).
   717→                         If a session has more timepoints than this, a random subset will be used.
   718→        svd_max_neurons: maximum number of neurons to use for SVD initialization (default: 2000).
   719→                         If a session has more neurons than this, random Gaussian projection will be used.
   720→                         The final weight is the product of the random projection and SVD matrices.
   721→        ncategories: optional list of length doutput giving number of categories for each output dimension.
   722→                     If not provided, will be inferred from data.
   723→        balanced_loss: if True, use class-weighted cross-entropy loss to compensate for class imbalance.
   724→                       Weights are inverse of class frequency. Default: False.
   725→
   726→    Returns:
   727→        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:
   728→            'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor of shape (npcs, nneurons[session])
   729→            'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension
   730→            'ncategories': list of length doutput, ncategories[out_dim] is the number of categories for that output
   731→            'device': torch device used for training
   732→
   733→    """
   734→
   735→    model = {
   736→        'projection': [],
   737→        'decoder': [],
   738→        'ncategories': [],
   739→        'device': None
   740→    }
   741→
   742→    npcs = kwargs.get('npcs', 10)
   743→    num_epochs = kwargs.get('num_epochs', 200)
   744→    lr = kwargs.get('lr', 0.001)
   745→    l1_weight = kwargs.get('l1_weight', 1e-4)
   746→    device_str = kwargs.get('device', None)
   747→    balanced_loss = kwargs.get('balanced_loss', False)
   748→
   749→    nsessions = len(neural)
   750→    if device_str is not None:
   751→        device = torch.device(device_str)
   752→    else:
   753→        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
   754→
   755→    model['device'] = device
   756→    print('Using device:', device)
   757→
   758→    # Prepare training data using helper function
   759→    session_data, dinput, doutput = _prepare_session_data(neural, input, output, device)
   760→
   761→    # Determine number of categories for each output dimension
   762→    if 'ncategories' in kwargs:
   763→        ncategories = kwargs['ncategories']
   764→    else:
   765→        ncategories = []
   766→        for out_dim in range(doutput):
   767→            max_cat = 0
   768→            for session in range(nsessions):
   769→                if session_data[session] is None:
   770→                    continue
   771→                max_cat = max(max_cat, int(session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].max().item()))
   772→            ncategories.append(max_cat + 1)
   773→
   774→    model['ncategories'] = ncategories
   775→
   776→    # Compute class weights (always, for use in chance computation and optionally for balanced loss)
   777→    class_weights = []
   778→    class_fractions = []  # Store fractions for chance computation
   779→    for out_dim in range(doutput):
   780→        # Count occurrences of each class across all sessions
   781→        class_counts = np.zeros(ncategories[out_dim])
   782→        for session in range(nsessions):
   783→            if session_data[session] is None:
   784→                continue
   785→            outputs = session_data[session]['output'][:, out_dim].cpu().numpy()
   786→            for c in range(ncategories[out_dim]):
   787→                class_counts[c] += np.sum(outputs == c)
   788→        # Store class fractions for chance computation
   789→        total = np.sum(class_counts)
   790→        fractions = class_counts / total
   791→        class_fractions.append(fractions)
   792→        # Compute weights as inverse of frequency (with smoothing to avoid division by zero)
   793→        weights = total / (ncategories[out_dim] * np.maximum(class_counts, 1))
   794→        # Normalize weights to sum to 1 (so each output dimension is equally weighted)
   795→        weights = weights / np.sum(weights)
   796→        class_weights.append(torch.tensor(weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=device))
   797→
   798→    model['class_weights'] = class_weights
   799→    model['class_fractions'] = class_fractions
   800→
   801→    if balanced_loss:
   802→        print(f"Using balanced loss with class weights:")
   803→        for out_dim in range(doutput):
   804→            print(f"  Output {out_dim}: {class_weights[out_dim].cpu().numpy()}")
   805→
   806→    # Initialize projection matrices for each session
   807→    svd_max_samples = kwargs.get('svd_max_samples', 50000)  # Max timepoints to use for SVD initialization
   808→    svd_max_neurons = kwargs.get('svd_max_neurons', 2000)   # Max neurons to use for SVD initialization
   809→    projection_layers = []
   810→    for session in range(nsessions):
   811→        nneurons = session_data[session]['nneurons']
   812→        proj = nn.Linear(nneurons, npcs, bias=False).to(device)
   813→
   814→        # Initialize with SVD for stability (use V from SVD of neural data)
   815→        # For neural data with shape (n_timepoints, n_neurons), SVD gives principal components in V
   816→        # Use random subsets if data is too large
   817→        n_timepoints = session_data[session]['neural'].shape[0]
   818→
   819→        # Sample timepoints if needed
   820→        if n_timepoints > svd_max_samples:
   821→            time_indices = torch.randperm(n_timepoints)[:svd_max_samples]
   822→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural'][time_indices, :]
   823→            print(f"Session {session}: Using {svd_max_samples} of {n_timepoints} timepoints for SVD initialization")
   824→        else:
   825→            neural_subset = session_data[session]['neural']
   826→
   827→        # Use random projection if too many neurons
   828→        if nneurons > svd_max_neurons:
   829→            # Create random Gaussian projection matrix: (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons)
   830→            P = torch.randn(nneurons, svd_max_neurons)
   831→            # Project neural data: (n_timepoints, n_neurons) @ (n_neurons, svd_max_neurons) = (n_timepoints, svd_max_neurons)
   832→            neural_projected = neural_subset @ P
   833→            print(f"Session {session}: Using random projection to {svd_max_neurons} of {nneurons} neurons for SVD initialization")
   834→
   835→            # SVD on projected data
   836→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_projected, some=True)
   837→            # V has shape (svd_max_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, svd_max_neurons))
   838→
   839→            # Compose: final weight = (P @ V[:, :npcs]).T = V[:, :npcs].T @ P.T
   840→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])
   841→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = (V[:, :n_components].T @ P.T).to(device).clone()
   842→        else:
   843→            # Standard SVD without random projection
   844→            _, _, V = torch.svd(neural_subset, some=True)
   845→            # V has shape (n_neurons, min(n_timepoints_subset, n_neurons))
   846→            n_components = min(npcs, V.shape[1])
   847→            proj.weight.data[:n_components, :] = V[:, :n_components].T.to(device).clone()
   848→
   849→        # Initialize remaining components randomly if needed
   850→        if n_components < npcs:
   851→            nn.init.orthogonal_(proj.weight.data[n_components:, :])
   852→
   853→        projection_layers.append(proj)
   854→
   855→    # Initialize separate decoders for each output dimension
   856→    decoders = []
   857→    for out_dim in range(doutput):
   858→        decoder = nn.Linear(npcs + dinput, ncategories[out_dim]).to(device)
   859→        decoders.append(decoder)
   860→
   861→    # Collect all parameters
   862→    all_params = []
   863→    for proj in projection_layers:
   864→        all_params.extend(proj.parameters())
   865→    for decoder in decoders:
   866→        all_params.extend(decoder.parameters())
   867→
   868→    optimizer = optim.Adam(all_params, lr=lr)
   869→
   870→    # Loss function with reduction='none' for manual weighting (matches torch_brain)
   871→    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='none')
   872→
   873→    # Training loop
   874→    # Data stays on CPU; each session is moved to GPU one at a time.
   875→    # backward() is called per session to free the computation graph before
   876→    # loading the next session. Gradients accumulate across sessions.
   877→    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
   878→        epoch_loss = 0.
   879→        optimizer.zero_grad()
   880→
   881→        for session in range(nsessions):
   882→            if session_data[session] is None:
   883→                continue
   884→            # Move this session's data to device
   885→            neural_batch = session_data[session]['neural'].to(device)
   886→            input_batch = session_data[session]['input'].to(device)
   887→            output_batch = session_data[session]['output'].to(device)
   888→
   889→            # Forward pass - shared projection
   890→            projected = projection_layers[session](neural_batch)
   891→            combined = torch.cat([projected, input_batch], dim=1)
   892→
   893→            # Compute loss for each output dimension
   894→            session_loss = torch.tensor(0., device=device)
   895→            for out_dim in range(doutput):
   896→                logits = decoders[out_dim](combined)
   897→                target = output_batch[:, out_dim]
   898→                loss_per_sample = criterion(logits, target)
   899→
   900→                if balanced_loss:
   901→                    # Manual per-sample weighting (matches torch_brain exactly)
   902→                    sample_weights = class_weights[out_dim][target]
   903→                    session_loss += (sample_weights * loss_per_sample).sum() / sample_weights.sum()
   904→                else:
   905→                    session_loss += loss_per_sample.mean()
   906→
   907→            # Add L1 regularization on current session's projection matrix
   908→            if l1_weight > 0:
   909→                l1_loss = torch.sum(torch.abs(projection_layers[session].weight))
   910→                session_loss += l1_weight * l1_loss
   911→
   912→            # Backward per session: frees computation graph, accumulates gradients
   913→            session_loss.backward()
   914→            epoch_loss += session_loss.item()
   915→
   916→        optimizer.step()
   917→
   918→        if ((epoch + 1) % 10 == 0) or (epoch < 10):
   919→            # Loss is sum of per-output-dim means across sessions
   920→            # Normalize by (nsessions * doutput) to get average per output per session
   921→            train_loss_normalized = epoch_loss / (nsessions * doutput)
   922→            print(f'Epoch [{epoch+1}/{num_epochs}], Loss: {train_loss_normalized:.6f}')
   923→
   924→    # Store trained parameters
   925→    for session in range(nsessions):
   926→        model['projection'].append(projection_layers[session].weight.data.clone())
   927→    model['decoder'] = decoders
   928→
   929→    return model

   931→def predict(neural: list, input: list, model: dict, sessionid: list | None = None, metadata: dict = {}):
   932→    """
   933→    Uses a trained decoder model to predict output from neural and input data.
   934→
   935→    Inputs:
   936→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list
   937→                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),
   938→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial
   939→        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of
   940→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
   941→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.
   942→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
   943→        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:
   944→                'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor
   945→                'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension
   946→                'ncategories': list of length doutput with number of categories per output dimension
   947→                'device': torch device
   948→        sessionid: optional list of length nsessions, giving the IDs of the sessions.
   949→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.
   950→    Returns:
   951→        predictions: list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
   952→                and predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int
   953→                with the predicted categorical output variable(s) for each timepoint.
   954→        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
   955→                and pcs[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (npcs, T[session][trial]) with the projected neural data.
   956→        confidences: list of length nsessions, confidences[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
   957→                and confidences[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) with the confidence scores.
   958→    """
   959→
   960→    nsessions = len(neural)
   961→    device = model['device']
   962→    decoders = model['decoder']
   963→    doutput = len(decoders)
   964→
   965→    # Replicate 1D inputs along time axis to match neural data (make copies to avoid modifying original)
   966→    input_processed = []
   967→    for session in range(nsessions):
   968→        input_session = []
   969→        for trial in range(len(neural[session])):
   970→            T = neural[session][trial].shape[1]  # time dimension
   971→
   972→            # Handle 1D input - replicate along time
   973→            if input[session][trial].ndim == 1:
   974→                input_trial = np.tile(input[session][trial][:, np.newaxis], (1, T))
   975→            else:
   976→                input_trial = input[session][trial]
   977→            input_session.append(input_trial)
   978→        input_processed.append(input_session)
   979→
   980→    # Use processed data instead of original
   981→    input = input_processed
   982→
   983→    confidences = []
   984→    predictions = []
   985→    pcs = []
   986→
   987→    with torch.no_grad():

  1030→def f1scores_all_sessions(all_predictions: list, output: list):
  1031→    """
  1032→    Concatenate all predictions and ground truth to compute F1 scores across all sessions and trials
  1033→    Inputs:
  1034→        all_predictions: list of length nsessions, all_predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
  1035→                and all_predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = bool
  1036→                with the predicted output variable(s) for each timepoint.
  1037→        output: the ground truth output for each trial. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of
  1038→                length ntrials[session], and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial])
  1039→                OR (doutput,) (scalar per trial), dtype = float32. with the output variable(s) for each timepoint.
  1040→    Returns:
  1041→        f1scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the F1 score for each output dimension
  1042→    """
  1043→    nsessions = len(all_predictions)
  1044→    all_pred_concat = []
  1045→    all_output_concat = []
  1046→    doutput = output[0][0].shape[0]
  1047→
  1048→    for session in range(nsessions):
  1049→        for trial in range(len(all_predictions[session])):
  1050→            # Predictions are always (doutput, T)
  1051→            pred_trial = all_predictions[session][trial].T  # (T, doutput)
  1052→            all_pred_concat.append(pred_trial)
  1053→
  1054→            # Output can be (doutput,) or (doutput, T)
  1055→            output_trial = output[session][trial]
  1056→            if output_trial.ndim == 1:
  1057→                # Scalar per trial: (doutput,) -> expand to (T, doutput) where all T are the same
  1058→                T = pred_trial.shape[0]
  1059→                output_trial_expanded = np.tile(output_trial[:, np.newaxis], (1, T)).T  # (T, doutput)
  1060→                all_output_concat.append(output_trial_expanded)
  1061→            else:
  1062→                # Time-varying: (doutput, T) -> (T, doutput)
  1063→                all_output_concat.append(output_trial.T)
  1064→
  1065→    # Concatenate all timepoints from all trials and all sessions
  1066→    all_pred_concat = np.vstack(all_pred_concat)  # (total_timepoints, doutput)
  1067→    all_output_concat = np.vstack(all_output_concat)  # (total_timepoints, doutput)
  1068→
  1069→    # Compute F1 score for each output dimension (macro average for multiclass)
  1070→    f1scores = np.zeros(doutput)
  1071→    for out_dim in range(doutput):
  1072→        f1scores[out_dim] = f1_score(all_output_concat[:, out_dim], all_pred_concat[:, out_dim], average='macro')
  1073→
  1074→    return f1scores

  1131→def cross_validate_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: str | None = None,
  1132→                           nsets: int = 5,
  1133→                           eval_fn=None,
  1134→                           **kwargs):
  1135→    """
  1136→    Cross-validates the decoder function. Performs nsets-fold cross-validation, training the decoder on nsets-1 sets and testing on
  1137→    the held-out set. Each cross-validation set contains 1/nsets of the trials from each session.
  1138→    Finds a random split of trials for each session into nsets sets, then, for each set, trains the decoder on the other nsets-1 sets and
  1139→    computes the predictions on the held out set.

  1141→    Inputs:
  1142→        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list

  1144→                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial

  1146→                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
  1147→                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.

  1150→                length ntrials[session], and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]),
  1151→                dtype = float32 or int. with the output variable(s) for each timepoint.
  1152→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.

  1154→                model = train_decoder(neural_train, input_train, output_train, metadata, **kwargs)
  1155→                Default: train_decoder_linear

  1161→                scores = eval_fn(predictions, output)

  1163→    kwargs are passed to train_decoder
  1164→    Returns:
  1165→        scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the evaluation metric for each output dimension
  1166→        predictions: list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
  1167→                and predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial])

  1169→        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],

  1173→        trial_splits: list of length nsessions, trial_splits[session] is a list of length nsets,
  1174→                trial_splits[session][set] is a numpy array with the trial indices for that set for that session.
  1175→    """
  1176→
  1177→    if eval_fn is None:
  1178→        eval_fn = accuracy_all_sessions
  1179→
  1180→    nsessions = len(neural)
  1181→
  1182→    # Create random splits of trials for each session
  1183→    trial_splits = []
  1184→    for session in range(nsessions):
  1185→        ntrials = len(neural[session])
  1186→        trial_indices = np.random.permutation(ntrials)
  1187→
  1188→        # Split trial indices into nsets
  1189→        split_indices = np.array_split(trial_indices, nsets)
  1190→        trial_splits.append(split_indices)
  1191→
  1192→    # Initialize storage for all predictions (will be filled in during cross-validation)
  1193→    all_predictions = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
  1194→    all_pcs = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
  1195→    all_confidences = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
  1196→
  1197→    # Perform cross-validation
  1198→    for test_set in tqdm.trange(nsets):
  1199→        # Create training and test data for this fold
  1200→        train_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1201→        train_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1202→        train_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1203→
  1204→        test_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1205→        test_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1206→        test_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1207→
  1208→        test_trial_indices = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
  1209→
  1210→        for session in range(nsessions):

  1228→        # Train decoder on training data

  1230→
  1231→        # Predict on test data

  1234→        # Store predictions in the correct positions
  1235→        for session in range(nsessions):
  1236→            for idx, trial_idx in enumerate(test_trial_indices[session]):

  1400→                test_loss += loss_per_sample.mean().item()
  1401→
  1402→    test_loss_normalized = test_loss / (n_test_sessions * doutput)
  1403→    print(f"Test Loss: {test_loss_normalized:.6f}")
  1404→
  1405→    # Compute evaluation metric on test data only
  1406→    test_predictions_only = get_trial_indices(all_predictions, test_indices)
  1407→    test_output_only = get_trial_indices(output, test_indices)
  1408→
  1409→    scores = eval_fn(test_predictions_only, test_output_only)
  1410→
  1411→    return scores, all_predictions, all_pcs, all_confidences, train_indices, test_indices, model, output, state

  1433→def _train_decoder_pca_logistic(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: dict = {}, **kwargs):

  1438→    projected neural data and input data.

  1440→    Inputs:

  1447→                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
  1448→        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
  1449→                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = bool with the
  1450→                binary output variable(s) for each timepoint. Use a one-hot encoding for multi-class outputs.
  1451→        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.
  1452→
  1453→        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:
  1454→        npcs: number of principal components to use (default: 10)
  1455→
  1456→    Returns:

  1458→            'pca': list of length nsessions, pca[session] is a PCA object fitted to the neural data of that session

  1460→

  1499→    output = output_processed

  1511→        input_concat = np.concatenate([input[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(input[session]))], axis=0).astype(np.float32)
  1512→        output_concat = np.concatenate([output[session][trial].T for trial in range(len(output[session]))], axis=0).astype(bool)
